slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A transversal crosses two lines at two points. It forms corresponding angles (same position at each crossing), alternate interior angles (between the lines, opposite sides of the transversal) and same-side interior angles.

Theorem: if alternate interior angles are equal, the lines are parallel. So are the lines if corresponding angles are equal, or if same-side interior angles are supplementary.

Proof: if the lines met at a point, they would form a triangle in which one of the equal angles is an exterior angle and the other is a remote interior angle. The Exterior Angle Inequality says those cannot be equal. So the lines do not meet.
